frequency_question: How often do such authorities successfully scale up initiated structural intervention programs to their target operational maximums within their designated timelines?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly announced, non-emergency, regularized market intervention or debt management scaling programs by G10 sovereign debt managers or central banks since 1995. Excludes emergency crisis liquidity facilities deployed overnight.

cases.name: Federal Reserve Large-Scale Asset Purchase (QE1 expansion)
Bank of England gilt purchase program scaling
Bank of Japan Quantitative and Qualitative Monetary Easing volume expansion
ECB Public Sector Purchase Programme volume ramp-up
US Treasury regularized buyback program initial rollout

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named instances covering major G10 structural program volume expansions; exhaustive for major programmatic scale-ups of this specific administrative design.
known_gaps: Excludes minor adjustments by smaller emerging market treasuries.
skeleton: 6 historical major sovereign debt/asset management scale-up instances tracked, representing 6 successful executions of announced structural program volume targets where principal intent was explicit.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 relevant comparable instances
validity_reason: Institutional behavior of sovereign debt managers regarding announced operational targets changes slowly across decades.
